_evidence_class: MEASURED (ours; the build was re-executed end to end and both artifacts were streamed and hashed)
task: Does re-running the recorded argv regenerate b1train_agents.jsonl.xz bit for bit?
verdict_long: Re-executing the recorded argv on the dev box regenerated the 317 MB B1 TRAIN agent join BIT FOR BIT. The decompressed stream is identical (the claim that matters) AND the .xz container is identical (the digest the receipts quote). No qualification is needed: this is form (1), not form (2).

headline_decompressed_stream._why_this_is_the_headline: .xz is not deterministic across preset/threads, so a container digest alone can neither prove nor disprove anything about the data. The decompressed stream is the claim a consumer cares about.
headline_decompressed_stream.tie_to_the_versioned_record: the COMMITTED sidecar's digest_scope.note names 8a9277a77b132e2631b133f9bea0758e as 'the other candidate' it hashed when deciding scope. Both the original AND the rebuild hash to exactly that, so the decompressed axis is pinned to a digest that is IN GIT -- not only to a local file.

container_beside_it.measured_by: GNU md5sum on the file, INDEPENDENT of the builder's own hashlib print (which also said 1c985e6d...)

xz_fingerprint_both.decoded: single stream, single block, filter 0x21 (LZMA2), dict 8 MiB, check CRC64 -- exactly lzma preset=6, single-threaded
xz_fingerprint_both.why_recorded: makes 'the compressor settings changed' a testable claim rather than an escape hatch

clipset_sha256.meaning: sha256 over the SORTED clip ids -- clip SET identity

key_seq_sha256.meaning: sha256 over (clip_id, frame) in FILE ORDER -- would catch a pure re-ordering

multiset_sha256.meaning: sha256 over the SORTED per-line digests -- content identity INDEPENDENT of row order; this is the 'sorted decompressed records' hash

controls._why: a verification that cannot fail proves nothing
controls.all_digests_full_length: 32 hex for every md5, 64 for every sha256 -- asserted before any comparison was allowed to return 'match'
controls.no_digest_is_the_empty_digest: d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e and e3b0c442...b855 both explicitly excluded
controls.comparator_not_stuck_on_equal: sha256('x') != sha256('y') asserted in the same breath
controls.dep_chain_control: 0 commits touched the 5 relevant modules since the build commit, against 34 commits total on the branch in that window -- the non-zero half proves the log was really read
controls.eol_comparator_control: two genuinely different source files hashed unequal, so the CR-stripping comparison is not stuck-on-equal

build_log_comparison._why: 4,602 lines of per-clip statistics are an independent, per-clip check that the JOIN ITSELF reproduced, not just the final digest
differences: the --out / meta PATHS in B1_JOIN_DONE (intended: --out was redirected)

the rebuild prints ONE EXTRA line: '[b1join] digest_scope declared: md5(compressed of ...) = 1c985e6d...'. The original build predates that print; its digest_scope was written post-hoc by backfill_digest_scope.py. See sidecar_differences.
build_log_comparison.identical_prefix: all 4,602 preceding lines are byte-identical, including every per-clip boxes/vis/dt/misjoin statistic, the ALIGNMENT GATE line (true_max=0.1872, misjoin+1 min=0.8193, sep=4.4x, PASS) and the per-clip gate line (EXCLUDED 7 of 4434 probed clips, 0.1579%)

sidecar_differences._why: the ARTIFACT is byte-identical; the SIDECAR is not, and saying so is the difference between an honest result and an overclaim

keys_that_differ.digest_scope.declared_by: 'backfill-MEASURED' -> 'build_b1_agent_join'; the DIGEST ITSELF is identical (1c985e6d...). The original's digest_scope was backfilled by backfill_digest_scope.py after the build; the current builder emits it natively.

on_disk_size_difference_is_LINE_ENDINGS.explanation: Path.write_text() translates \n to \r\n on Windows, so the builder writes CRLF; the original file was rewritten LF by backfill_digest_scope.py. Re-serialised at indent=1 the two are 4,482,188 vs 4,482,109 UTF-8 bytes -- a 79-byte difference that is entirely the digest_scope note above.
on_disk_size_difference_is_LINE_ENDINGS.warning: this is the same core.autocrlf trap that made 174 pod files look like drift; a size delta of one CR per line is NOT a content delta

reproduction_recipe_as_executed.code_tree: git -c core.autocrlf=false -c core.eol=lf archive HEAD stack taniteval, extracted to a PRIVATE dir; every module verified at runtime to resolve inside it

risks_found: b1_train_plus_eval_agents.jsonl.xz -- the file the launch reads -- has NO sidecar and its digest was unrecorded until this file
CONTROL_b1eval_recon.jsonl.xz (10,012,564 B, md5 3ddb42ecbd3926066795a94587af2aed) has ONE loose copy plus two embedded ones; it is the thin part of the chain, not the 317 MB part

.gitignore matches NO rule for the 317 MB artifact (git check-ignore exit 1; control: __pycache__/ correctly matches at .gitignore:2). One cp into a raw/ dir plus a routine git add would put 317 MB into history irreversibly. A '*.jsonl.xz' rule with a '!*.meta.json' exception closes it in one line.
the SHARED git index holds a stale OLDER blob (ddacde6a) for stack/scripts/build_b1_agent_join.py while the worktree equals HEAD exactly; known mm_commit.py side effect; REPORTED, NOT UNSTAGED
mount_incidents: cp to G: refused with 'File exists' while stat on the same path in the same breath said 'No such file or directory', and the file was genuinely absent. One retry landed it, verified by git hash-object. A failed write on this mount is not evidence of anything.

reading the 4.48 MB committed sidecar off G: failed 4x (OSError Errno 22 / 'Invalid request code') and cp left a 0-byte local file. The file is intact -- reading it from the git object database returned all 4,482,188 bytes. A failed read on this mount is NOT evidence of absence.
answer_to_the_question: YES, it is safe for this artifact to stay out of git. It is now REPRODUCIBLE BY RE-EXECUTION, not merely by construction: the recorded argv, the committed builder and the committed clip list regenerate it bit for bit, and the only unversioned inputs are ~4.1 GB of upstream PhysicalAI parquets whose re-pull script is itself committed. Two durable copies plus a proven recipe is a sound margin; a 317 MB binary in git would not be. The residual risk is not the TRAIN join at all -- it is the UNDOCUMENTED derived file the launch actually reads, and the missing .gitignore guard.
